thread:
katherine: Ok—heads up: we’re planning the release-sentinel cutover tonight 02:00 PT. This includes kernel v3.2.1 (ABI bump) + quant build q128. Need quick alignment on rollback criteria, pin TTL, release-note copy, and who owns the immediate rollback.
ryan: 02:00 PT works for me. Canary plan?
minju: Canary at 1% traffic for 20m, then 10% for 30m if green. Keep staged holdback for the first hour.
ops-lin: I can own operator rollback. Trigger if any of these happen: errors >5% sustained for 5m, p95 latency +30% vs baseline for 10m, or kv-cache hit-rate drop >15%.
katherine: +1 on those thresholds. Add memory OOM spike: any OOM in prod feed -> immediate rollback.
ryan: Also watch for inference-quality regressions: customer-facing prompt evals failing NIST set >2 regressions -> abort. We'll run eval set during canary.
minju: Pin TTL request: extend default pin TTL to 4h for the night window so deploybot stickiness doesn't expire mid-handoff.
ops-lin: Agreed. If we extend TTL, ops will do manual unpin after 4h if everything looks ok.
minju: Deploy commands I’ll run for the cutover:
```
# set sentinel canary
deploybot schedule --target=kernel-v3.2.1 --variant=q128 --canary=1% --start=2026-03-21T02:00:00-07:00
# pin for night window (TTL seconds)
deploybot pin --target=kernel-v3.2.1 --ttl=14400
```
katherine: Release notes blurb draft (short): "Runtime: kernel v3.2.1 (ABI-safe) and quant q128 — improves throughput for long-context models, introduces memory-usage optimizations. Observability: added p95 and kv-cache histograms for canary. If you see increased memory or latency, please contact eng-runtime immediately." Thoughts?
ryan: Clean. Add a short migration note: "Operators: kernel ABI bump may require model-vendor shim; fallback to compat-bridge if necessary."
minju: Also mention that small discrepancies in float outputs expected with q128 -> include link to eval report: https://internal/reports/quant-q128-canary-2026-03-20
ops-lin: Who’s running the eval harness during the canary?
katherine: Ryan will own the automated eval job and I’ll monitor dashboards. Ops will be on standby for rollback.
ryan: I’ll kick off the eval job 10m before canary start and stream results to #eng-runtime-monitoring.
deploy-bot: Scheduled: kernel-v3.2.1 (variant=q128) — canary 1% @ 2026-03-21T02:00:00-07:00. Pin applied (TTL=14400s).
minju: Small request — add a soft-fallback mapping so requests automatically route to quant64 if quant128 fails for a region:
```
routing:set fallback quant128 -> quant64 region=* priority=low
```
ops-lin: Good call. Ops will verify fallback after canary ramps.
katherine: Final checklist for tonight:
- [ ] deploybot scheduled & pin TTL extended
- [ ] eval harness running + baseline collected
- [ ] canary smoke (errors/latency/memory) gating rules active
- [ ] fallback mapping in place
- [ ] release notes published to internal release page
If anything trips these gates we roll back to kernel v3.1.x and unpin.
ryan: One last note — increase logging level for canary backends to capture stack traces for any inference failures (rotate after 2h).
ops-lin: Ops will be ready. I'll post rollback runbook in thread 30m before start.
katherine: thanks — if no objections I’ll proceed. :thumbsup:
ryan: :+1:
minju: :eyes:
deploy-bot: Confirmed scheduled action executed. Will post progress updates in this thread during the window.
